title: [GA4] Event collection limits
supports: Opened with WebFetch; no page date shown. No limit on distinct event names for web streams, 500 per app user for app streams; 25 parameters per event; event and parameter names 40 characters; parameter values 100 characters (page_location 1,000); 25 user properties; User-ID 256 characters.

title: [GA4] Recommended events
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Recommended event names for all properties (sign_up, login, search, share, generate_lead and others) and for online sales (view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase, refund and others); they are not sent automatically and should carry the prescribed parameters.

title: [GA4] Analytics 360 versus standard properties
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Standard vs 360 limits: 25 vs 100 parameters per event; 50 vs 125 event-scoped custom dimensions; 30 vs 50 key events; retention up to 14 vs 50 months; BigQuery daily export 1M events vs billions; 360 billing starts with a 360 contract.

title: [GA4] Funnel exploration
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Open vs closed funnels; up to 10 steps; 'directly' vs 'indirectly followed by'; Within time limit per step; breakdown by first value; next action shows top 5; trended funnel; users counted for their first sequence in the date range.

title: [GA4] Cohort exploration
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Inclusion and return criteria; daily, weekly (Sunday to Saturday) and monthly granularity; standard, rolling and cumulative calculations; maximum 60 cohorts; breakdown shows top 15 values; thresholding on demographic dimensions.

title: [GA4] Data retention
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Standard properties keep user-level and event data for 2 or 14 months; 360 can keep event data 26, 38 or 50 months; the setting affects only explorations and funnel reports; shortening removes data at the next monthly deletion; 24-hour delay before a change applies.

title: Best practices to avoid sending Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Google forbids sending data it could use or recognise as PII; URLs, titles, search terms, custom dimensions, campaign parameters and User-ID are higher risk; data redaction removes emails on a best-effort basis (web streams); no location finer than 1 square mile.

title: [GA4] BigQuery Export
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Standard properties have a daily export limit of 1 million events; streaming export is best-effort with no completeness SLO; Fresh Daily is 360 only; query events_YYYYMMDD rather than the intraday table; exports can go to the free BigQuery sandbox within its limits.

title: Consent mode overview
supports: Opened with WebFetch; no date shown. Consent types ad_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization and analytics_storage; basic mode blocks tags until consent; advanced mode sends cookieless pings when consent is denied; behavioural modelling needs a data threshold.

title: Google Analytics MCP server (googleanalytics/google-analytics-mcp)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. MCP server under the googleanalytics GitHub organisation using the Admin and Data APIs; read-only by default with the analytics.readonly scope; run_report and run_funnel_report tools; write tools (annotations, custom dimensions, key events) only with --allow-write and analytics.edit. No version or date shown.

title: Data planning playbook
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Taxonomy built in three steps from business objectives to user actions to events; event names are case-sensitive ('Song Played' vs 'song played'); one consistent syntax; one event with a property beats near-duplicate events; same property on every funnel step; event vs user properties.

title: Build a funnel analysis
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Step order options: this order, any order and exact order (no other events between steps); exclusion of users who did an event between steps; segments apply to the starting event.

title: Interpret your retention analysis
supports: Opened with WebFetch. N-day (Return On), unbounded (Return On or After) and bracket (custom) retention; unbounded sits higher than N-day; day 0 is the start day at 100%; days can be 24-hour windows or calendar dates; up to 100 brackets.

title: Amplitude MCP server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. OAuth over streamable HTTP; US and EU server URLs; reads and queries charts, funnels and retention; can create and edit charts, dashboards, cohorts, flags and taxonomy (deletes need two-step confirmation); per-project Use MCP (read) and (write) permissions; Enterprise included, Plus add-on, not on Free or Growth.

title: Create a tracking plan
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A tracking plan is a living source of truth; method: define and prioritise KPIs, map each KPI to user flows, translate flows into events and properties; warns against tracking every possible action; templates by industry.

title: Funnels: advanced
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Default conversion window 7 days, maximum 366 days; uniques, totals and sessions counting; specific or any order; hold up to 3 properties constant; exclusion steps cannot be first or last; default evaluates only the first entry, optimised re-entry evaluates all.

title: Retention
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 'On or After' is the default retention criterion, 'On' is stricter; rolling vs calendar day buckets; incomplete buckets marked with an asterisk; averages weighted and use completed periods only; day reports limited to 60 days; frequency view.

title: Mixpanel MCP Server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. OAuth sign-in and beta service accounts; US, EU and India endpoints; runs insights, funnels, flows and retention and can create and edit dashboards and Lexicon; not read-only; changes recorded in the audit log; enabled by default only for free and growth accounts created after 1 Aug 2026, otherwise an admin enables it; 600 requests per hour per user.

title: Product analytics best practices
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Lowercase snake_case, category:object_action names with present-tense verbs; is_/has_ booleans; no values in names; version events when flows change; consistent IDs and identify() timing; backend tracking for critical numbers; reverse proxy; out-of-order events; filter internal users.

title: Funnels
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Sequential, strict and any-order steps; conversion window; exclusion steps remove users from the whole funnel; breakdown attribution first touchpoint by default; correlation analysis; time to convert; trends with 'Hide incomplete periods'.

title: Retention
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Start and return events; recurring, first time and first ever occurrence; 'On' is the default returning criterion, 'On or after' is cumulative; weighted mean by default; percentages relative to period 0 by default or to the previous period.

title: Experiments
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Experiments are backed by feature flags that randomise users and record exposure; Bayesian or frequentist statistics; funnel, mean or ratio metrics from existing events; managed in the app, through an MCP client or the API.

title: Data Collection Best Practices (Tracking Plan)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (the segment.com copy returned 403 and was not bypassed). Object Action naming; Title Case event names and snake_case properties; never create event names or property keys dynamically; put detail in properties (Workspace Created with account_tier); start small and tie events to objectives.

title: How Not To Run an A/B Test
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 18 April 2010, calculator added May 2013. Stopping at the first significant reading gave 26.1% false positives in his simulation; fix the sample size in advance or use sequential or Bayesian designs; rule of thumb n = 16 sigma squared over delta squared.

title: Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in A/B Testing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 14 September 2020 (Fabijan and others). About 6% of Microsoft A/B tests have an SRM; chi-square test with a p-value threshold of 0.0005; causes at assignment, execution, log processing, analysis and experimenter stages; do not trust results until the cause is fixed.

title: Organ donor registrations: trialling different approaches
publisher: GOV.UK (Cabinet Office, Behavioural Insights Team, DHSC, DVLA, NHS Blood and Transplant)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; published 24 December 2013. The linked PDF was read as text: eight variants for five weeks, 1,085,322 people observed; reciprocity message best; group photo variant lowered sign-ups; 1,203 more registrations than control during the trial, about 96,000 a year estimated.

title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
publisher: EUR-Lex, Publications Office of the European Union
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Article 5(1)(b) purpose limitation, 5(1)(c) data minimisation ('adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary'), 5(1)(e) storage limitation; Recital 78 lists minimising processing among data protection by design and by default measures.

title: Sheet n°16: Use analytics on your websites and applications
supports: Opened with WebFetch; dated 11 June 2020. Analytics trackers need consent unless exempt; exemption conditions include audience measurement and A/B testing only, no cross-referencing, one publisher, last byte of IP removed, 13-month tracer lifetime; most large analytics offerings do not qualify; rules vary by EU country.

title: FTC Enforcement Action to Bar GoodRx from Sharing Consumers' Sensitive Health Info for Advertising
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 1 February 2023: GoodRx shared medications and health conditions with Facebook, Google, Criteo and others since at least 2017; $1.5 million civil penalty under the Health Breach Notification Rule; proposed order bans health data sharing for advertising and sets retention limits.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Hosted server at mcp.posthog.com; routes to the US or EU region by login; covers analytics queries, SQL, feature flags, experiments and error tracking; free to call, but some tools use LLMs billed as PostHog AI spend. The page does not describe a read-only mode.
